dataset.name: Sentinel-1 Radiometrically Terrain Corrected
dataset.provider: ESA / Copernicus; terrain correction by Catalyst for Microsoft
dataset.processing_level: GRD, radiometrically terrain corrected gamma-nought (linear power)
dataset.attribution: Contains modified Copernicus Sentinel data, processed by Catalyst

provenance.method: VV backscatter from one relative orbit: the median of the passes before (and after), and the lowest value of the passes in the flood window, which maps the largest extent seen. A pixel is flooded when VV during the flood period is below -17.0 dB, VV before was not, and VV fell by at least 3 dB. Pixels below the threshold before the flood are reported as pre-existing water.
provenance.speckleFilter: none: the working grid already averages many looks

landCover.name: ESA WorldCover 2021 v200
landCover.attribution: © ESA WorldCover project 2021 / Contains modified Copernicus Sentinel data

provenance.uncertainty: No accuracy assessment has been made against ground or optical reference data. Known error sources: wind-roughened water is missed; smooth dry surfaces and radar shadow can be mistaken for water; water under vegetation or between buildings is not detected, so flooding in dense crops and built-up areas is underestimated. thresholdSensitivity shows the effect of a 1 dB threshold error.

warnings: The backscatter histogram did not separate water from land clearly (Otsu separability 0.751), so a fixed threshold of -17 dB was used. This usually means water covers only a small share of the area. Check the result against the radar images.
The flooded area changes by more than half when the threshold moves by 1 dB either way. Treat the total as approximate.
